sources.title: Therapeutic Goods (Poisons Standard—October 2026) Instrument 2026, also cited as the Standard for the Uniform Scheduling of Medicines and Poisons No. 51 (s 1(2))
sources.publisher: Federal Register of Legislation (Australian Government); administered by the Department of Health, Disability and Ageing; made under para 52D(2)(b) of the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989
sources.version: F2026L01327, as made 28 Sep 2026, registered 30 Sep 2026; whole instrument commences 1 Oct 2026 (s 2); repeals the June 2026 Standard (F2026L00633) (s 4); FRL status 'In force', compilation number 0, no amendments or compilations registered as at 17 Oct 2026
sources.how: WebFetch of the FRL HTML (EPUB) and PDF: both stop at about 85,000-89,000 characters (Part 2, ss 34-47), before the Schedules (PDF pp. 280-298) and Index (p. 369). Reader's guide and ss 1-7 read twice and compared by script. Index lines were confirmed by exact-phrase searches of the official text through the FRL API (titles/search, filtered to F2026L01327), each decisive phrase searched twice in differently built queries and compared by script.
sources.note: The Index is not part of this instrument (s 5(2)). States and territories give effect to the scheduling through their own laws (Reader's guide); state laws were not read.

unsettled: Method: the Schedules and the Index of the Poisons Standard could not be read as text with WebFetch (both the FRL HTML and PDF stop in Part 2). Every status here comes from exact-phrase searches of the official text, which match lines of the Index (name, cross-reference line, then 'Schedule N' lines). The Index is not part of the instrument (s 5(2)), and no Schedule entry or its conditions was read. All rows are therefore draft, even where two searches agree; editor to decide whether two agreeing searches may count as ai-checked, or to have Schedules 4, 8, 9 and 10 and the Index read in a browser.

Cannabis, delta-9-THC (dronabinol), mescaline, psilocin and MDPV are named in the Standard, but the Schedule lines of their Index entries were not reached. The cannabis entry begins 'cannabis cross reference cannabis sativa hemp ...'.

CAS-only lines. 2C-I (CAS 69587-11-7) and 2C-T-7 (CAS 207740-26-9) are not named, but their CAS numbers are followed by 'Schedule 9' in the Index. JWH-018 (CAS 209414-07-3) is the same. CAS identity was not confirmed from an official source: NIST was rate-limited for 69587-11-7 and has no record of the other two. alpha-PVP (14530-33-7) and MDEA (82801-81-8) are similar, but no Schedule was found after their CAS numbers. CAS numbers were tried only as search keys; for 2C-B, 1,4-butanediol, GHB and psilocybine the identity is from NIST.

Several statuses come from a cross-reference list of an Index entry whose own name was not read: DMT, MDMA, MDA, salvinorin A, mephedrone, GHB, 2C-B and 1,4-butanediol. Each line carries that name or CAS number and ends in the Schedule(s) given.

Group entries exist but their text was not read: '...cannabinomimetics' (Schedule 9) and '...cathinones' (Schedule 9). The words 'phenethylamine', 'phenylethylamine' and 'benzodiazepine' also occur. Combined with s 7(c) (derivatives), these may cover the not-found synthetic cannabinoids, cathinones, 2C-E, 2C-C, 5-MeO-DMT, the benzodiazepines etizolam and flualprazolam, the fentanyl analogues and 7-hydroxymitragynine. Not-found rows stay draft until those entries are read.
Absence (not-found) tests were read once only, because the FRL API stopped answering before the second reading. The Schedule 9 alternative for amfetamine was also checked once only.
Exclusion of Schedules 2, 3, 5, 6, 7 and 10 (and 4 for the Schedule 8 drugs) rests on one reading of grouped searches. The Schedule 8 or 9 alternative and the end of each Index line were read twice.
PSILOCYBINE's Index cross-reference gives CAS No. 520-52-5 for 'PSILOCYBIN'; NIST gives 520-52-5 as psilocybine, so this is consistent.
